newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse awaits post-Thanksgiving moves.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse awaits post-Thanksgiving moves.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended down on Wednesday after initial hopes that cyclical stocks could push up the Bel-20 index faded, but dealers said an inflow of cash in December would lift the index once more.
"Normally we'd see a lot of buying tomorrow as new accounts are opened but as the U.S. goes into Thanksgiving and investors go on holiday, it'll stay quiet," a dealer said.
He added investors would stay in 'wait and see' mode until U.S. players returned on Monday.
The Bel-20 closed down 0.59 percent, or 11.11 points, at 1,869.59 after Tuesday's record high of 1,880.70.
One dealer said bourse volumes would slip unless the Dow posted a record high overnight.
"In December a lot of money will come onto the market from bonuses and pension funds," a dealer said.
Traditionally December and January were good bourse months and the index could rise to new records again, he added.
Institutions kept a low profile in Wednesday's trade, trading few baskets, and seemed to take profits on insurance stocks.
"When a firm in the insurance sector suffers profittaking you often get a snowball effect in the rest of the financial sector, that has happened today," said one trader.
Dealers said financials were suffering after recent bull runs, but were expected then to bounce back into the limelight in coming weeks.
Among insurers Fortis AG, due to post nine-month results on Thursday, shed 2.4 percent to 4,840 francs. Royale Belge lost 2.3 percent to 6,460 francs.
In the banking sector BBL was down 0.5 percent at 6,600 francs, Kredietbank lost 0.5 percent to 10,250 francs.
Cyclicals, which rose in recent days after having lagged the index, suffered from the Dow's fall despite low interest rates and a positive economic outlook for Belgium in 1997.
Maritime transporter CMB fell 1.5 percent to 2,380 francs and steel cord and wire maker Bekaert was down 0.7 percent at 26,275 francs.
Dealers said only a strong correction on the Dow could keep the index jumping ahead again in coming weeks.
